subject: Phased GPU onramp & s-curve commit proposal for FjordTech (Dedicated)
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fjordtech.ai>, FjordTech Procurement <procurement@fjordtech.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Our internal model shows substantial burst requirements for inference in Q4 tied to a new feature launch; we expect TPMS to rise quickly but steady out by Q2 next year. Procurement asked that we get three things from Redwood to move ahead:

- A clean example of a multi-year prepaid schedule with term discounts tied to committed TPM/GPU counts
- A phased ramp (S-curve) option that eases cash outflows in year 1 but still gives us better unit economics at steady state
- Any constraints around minimum commitment timing for Dedicated (can we shift capacity between quarters?)

Attached is a demand forecast and the RFP appendix. Can you propose a draft ramp schedule and highlight where discounts apply?

Cheers,
Ellie
Head of Product
FjordTech

Attachments: FjordTech_Demand_Forecast_Q4.pdf, RFP-security-appendix.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Ellie —

Thanks for the forecast. Karthik and I reviewed it and put together two high-level approaches you can consider: a 3-year prepaid with graduated discounts and a 1+2 structure (one year prepay + two years annual renewals with volume bands). Key tradeoffs: bigger up-front prepay = deeper term discount; phased ramp helps cashflow but delays larger discounts until you hit committed tiers.

I attached a proposed term schedule (Redwood_Term_Schedule_v3.xlsx). Karthik, can you confirm whether we can allow quarter-to-quarter reallocation inside the first 12 months?

Next steps: I can convert the schedule into a succinct mutual action plan once we align on target commitment curve. Would you prefer a steeper S-curve in Q1–Q2 or a flatter ramp with higher later-year commitment?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Term_Schedule_v3.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Ellie, Vanessa —

Short answer: yes, we can support intra-quarter reallocation in year 1 up to a capped % of the committed pool (we typically allow +/- 20% per quarter to accommodate bursty usage). For multi-quarter shifts beyond that we treat them as amendments (no problem, just need 30 days notice).

A few notes on discounting:
- Baseline: 0% term discount on monthly pay-as-you-go Dedicated.
- 12-month prepaid: up to 12% discount at our standard annual tiers.
- 36-month prepaid: up to 22% discount for the top-tier commitments.
- We can add step-up discounts tied to hitting TPM/GPU milestones (e.g., +3% when you reach 60% of the committed capacity for 2 consecutive months).

Marissa will run a scenario with your forecast to show the effective blended unit price under a conservative and aggressive S-curve. Expect that by EOD Friday.

Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fjordtech.ai>, FjordTech Procurement <procurement@fjordtech.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Thanks Karthik — that flexibility on reallocation helps. Two clarifying points from Tom (cc):

1) Procurement wants to avoid large overhangs where we prepay, but usage never materializes. Are there short-circuit clauses (credits or return-of-capacity) if FjordTech misses committed thresholds by year 2?
2) From a cashflow POV, is there an intermediate structure where we prepay 40% in year 1 (gets a mid-tier discount), then 30% in year 2, 30% in year 3 — but with a soft true-up mechanism if we exceed commitments?

Ellie

On a related note, Tom asked if Redwood can show a worked example: baseline monthly vs 3-year prepaid vs 3-year prepaid with step-up credits. That would really help procurement and the CFO.

—
Ellie

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Ellie/Tom/Vanessa/Karthik —

Attached are two worked scenarios based on your forecast:

1) S-curve conservative (40% Y1 / 35% Y2 / 25% Y3) — effective blended discount: 11.2% across committed TPMs, with an allowance to shift +/-20% per quarter in Y1. No refunds for unused committed capacity; unused prepay converts to account credit valid for 12 months.

2) Aggressive step-up (25% Y1 / 35% Y2 / 40% Y3 with step-up +3% at 60% utilization) — effective blended discount: 15.7% if milestones achieved. We also included a soft true-up: if you exceed committed capacity, you get pro-rated overage credit applied to next billing cycle, and if you underutilize by >30% vs commit at end of Y2, we offer 50% of the remaining prepay as credit back to FjordTech (requires executive sign-off).

Key commercial terms included in the spreadsheet: payment schedule, milestone definitions, notice periods for reallocations, and audit/usage reporting cadence.

Attachment: worked_examples_Scurve_vs_stepup.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

P.S. I put a short summary in the HubSpot record HS-987654. I'll follow up with a concise MAP for signatures once you pick the structure.

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fjordtech.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellie Park <ellie@fjordtech.ai>, FjordTech Procurement <procurement@fjordtech.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and ask for phased onramp options

Marissa/Vanessa/Karthik —

Appreciate the scenarios, Marissa. Procurement likes the conservative S-curve (40/35/25) but wants the soft true-up language tightened: specifically we need a spelled-out formula for the 50% return-of-prepay (how the remaining balance is calculated, timing, and who signs off). Also need clear SLA credits if Dedicated latency/service targets aren't met in year 1 during burst windows.

Can you put together a short amendment (1 page) with the calculation and proposed SLA credit schedule? If we can get that in the next week, Procurement will fast-track legal review.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
VP Engineering
FjordTech
